BLOCKED (determinate). The dot-pattern expectancy / AX-CPT task is a nonverbal cognitive task: there is no published item wording to transcribe. The 24 live item codes are stimulus conditions, _, where condition is the AX/AY/BX/BY cue-probe validity class and probeN names one of six dot-pattern PNG images (probe1.png..probe6.png). Two facts make item_text unrecoverable rather than merely unlocated. (1) The stimuli are images with no text: expfactory-experiments/dot_pattern_expectancy/experiment.js renders each trial as , so any item_text would be an invented description of a picture. (2) The probe identity is randomised per participant: experiment.js shuffles ['probe1.png'..'probe6.png'] and pops valid_probe per session, so which PNG plays the valid 'X' role differs by respondent -- confirmed in the raw data, where all 3,130 worker x probe combinations map to exactly one of X/Y within a worker while every probe appears under all four conditions across workers. probeN therefore has no stable semantic content that any text could state. The only stable, meaningful part of the code (AX/AY/BX/BY) is already self-describing. The task instructions ARE published in experiment.js, but they too embed the participant-specific valid cue/probe images ('The target pair is shown below:' followed by two tags), and a 24-row file carrying instructions with item_text and option_text blank for every row would carry no item referent -- the irw#1770 bar. option_text is separately unavailable: resp is trial accuracy (0/1) computed by the processing script, not a chosen response option. No CSV written. RETRY TEST: would an unchanged retry, right now, plausibly produce a different result? NO -- determinate verdict (nonverbal image stimuli, no wording published anywhere, and a per-participant-randomised stimulus role that no single item_text could state). To flip it, the schema would have to admit image stimuli or an item-level stimulus-description convention for cognitive tasks; a new source cannot supply wording that does not exist.

There is no text in any stimulus, so no `item_text` exists to transcribe and none can be written without IRW authoring prose. `option_text` is likewise empty: resp is behaviour-scored accuracy. An items.csv here would be 8 rows of blank item_text and blank option_text -- the shape gilbert_meta_39 was excluded for and twod_rotation_mather2023 was held from upload for -- while making the table count as having item text in irw_list_itemtext_tables(). WHAT IS RECOVERABLE, recorded so an unblock needs no re-investigation: (a) the verbatim whole-task instructions from experiment.js, 'On each trial of this experiment a red or blue box will appear. If you see a red box, press the [X]. If you see a blue box, press the [Y]. We will start with practice where you will get feedback about whether you responded correctly. We will begin after you end the instructions.' -- where [X]/[Y] is 'left arrow'/'right arrow' in an order shuffled per participant (var correct_responses = jsPsych.randomization.shuffle([['left arrow',37],['right arrow',39]])), so no single administered instruction sentence exists for the table; and (b) a per-item correct_response that IS exactly determined by the code -- congruent items require the arrow key on the same side as the box, incongruent items the opposite arrow (confirmed in the raw file: *_left_congruent and *_right_incongruent -> keycode 37 left arrow; *_right_congruent and *_left_incongruent -> keycode 39 right arrow, with no exceptions across 67,300 test trials). The item codes were proved to mean what they say rather than assumed: re-running the processing script's item construction over the two raw GitHub files reproduces all 8 per-item n exactly against irw_table_sets() (8600/8225/8225/8600/8225/8600/8600/8225), and accuracy splits congruent 0.973-0.975 vs incongruent 0.930-0.938, the expected Simon effect. Note the availability audit (availability_audit_full.csv) marked this AVAILABLE on the reasoning that 'the stimulus/design is fully reconstructable from the well-known paradigm description' -- that is a reconstruction-from-general-knowledge argument, not a transcript, and it is the reasoning itemtext_standard.md rules out. RETRY TEST: NO. An unchanged retry would find the same task source and the same absence of per-item wording. What would flip it is a policy decision (extending the cogcontrol_gyurkovics_2019_flanker precedent) that whole-task instructions plus an IRW-authored stimulus description are shippable for trial-level cognitive tasks; the material to do that is already in hand and quoted above.
